sections.html:
The Recorder of Deeds is in the Platte County Administration Building at 415 Third St., Room 035, Platte City, MO 64079. Call (816) 858-3326. A second line, (816) 858-1832, is also listed.

The counter keeps two schedules. Searching records and buying copies is open from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., lunch hour included. New documents are accepted for recording only from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. County closures this year fall on Thursday and Friday, November 26 and 27, and on December 24 and 25.

sections.h2: What the recorder does in a home sale
sections.html:
The recorder keeps the county's permanent land records. The office records real estate transactions, files state and federal tax liens, holds military discharge papers and issues marriage licenses. When a Platte County house sells, the deed to the buyer is recorded here, and so is the release a lender files after its loan is paid off.

Uniform Commercial Code filings are not handled here, because the Missouri Secretary of State has taken them since July 1, 2001. Only the DD214 disclaimer form needs a formal request. For other documents, phone or email and staff will pull them without a Sunshine request. Formal requests go to the custodian of records at extension 3326 of the main number.

Real estate and marriage records are public, while divorce records sit with the Circuit Clerk. Marriage license applications are taken from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

Expect $26 for the first page and $3 for every page after it when the document meets the standards. A statewide fee increase now applies to recorded documents, marriage licenses and plats, and the schedule below is the one in use. Overpayments are not refunded, so a phone call for the exact total is worth the time.

Platte County recorder charges
Document or serviceFee
Standard real estate document, first page$26.00
Each page after the first$3.00
Non-standard document, first page$51.00
Plat or survey, first page$71.00
Plat or survey, each added page$50.00
Recorded document copy, per page$1.00
Certification of a copy$1.00

A document that releases or assigns more than one item adds $5 for each extra item. The marriage license fee is $53, paid in exact cash or by card with a convenience fee.

Missing the Recorders Association of Missouri layout rules adds a $25 charge, which is the gap between $26 and $51 on page one. The rules date from January 1, 2002, and a title company or attorney will normally build them into the deed form. A seller drafting a deed alone should check each item.

  • Letter-size paper that is white or light, 20-pound, with no logos or watermarks.
  • Dark ink on one side, with type of at least 8 points.
  • The top 3 inches of page one left empty for the recorder's stamp, and three-quarter inch margins elsewhere.
  • A typed, stamped or printed name under every signature.
  • No tape or staples holding attachments to a page, other than a secure bar-coded label.

Page one must show the title, the date, each grantor with marital status, each grantee, statutory addresses and the legal description. The words grantor and grantee must appear so the instrument can be indexed, and a street address is not accepted as a legal description. The county formatting page at co.platte.mo.us/formatting has the full list.

sections.h2: Documents exempt from the formatting rules
sections.html:
Several kinds of paper are exempt and pay only the per-page fee. Documents signed before January 1, 2002 are one group. The others are military separation papers, documents signed outside the United States, certified copies, judgments or papers shaped to court rules, and fixture filings on national approved forms. A document is also exempt when one of the original parties has died or is incapacitated.

A cover sheet is optional, but one that is used is recorded as page one and must have the 3-inch top margin and the first-page information. A paper sent in for re-recording needs a new first page or cover sheet meeting the same rules. Rejected documents come back with a reason stated.

The recorder's iRecord portal at plattemo.icounty.com handles searches, and the same site runs a free Record Notification Service. Register for a free account, confirm the email link, choose your criteria, and the system sends a message whenever a matching deed is recorded.

An owner can set the alert on their own name, which helps catch a fraudulent filing early. The county adds that its online data is not official and does not replace professional advice. Online search pricing belongs to the portal, so ask the office or read the site before relying on any number.

sections.h2: Is there a transfer tax on a Platte County deed?
sections.html:
The recorder's schedule lists recording, copy and plat charges and has no line for a transfer tax. For tax advice on a sale, call a title company or Missouri attorney. The recorder at (816) 858-3326 can tell you what the office itself collects when it accepts a deed.

Property tax is a separate matter. The Platte County Collector bills it, with statements due on receipt and delinquent after December 31. The Assessor's office also lists a sales validation and education coordinator at (816) 858-1256, a useful number when a sale price needs to be explained to the county.

Platte County is part of the Kansas City metro area. The July 2025 estimate is 114,400 residents and 47,969 housing units. A typical owned home is worth $345,100, owners occupy 67.4 percent of homes and 425 building permits were issued in 2025. The county was organized on December 31, 1838, and the Platte City courthouse carries a National Register listing. Because new documents are accepted only until 4 p.m., send a deed early in the day.

sections.h2: From deed to recorded record, step by step
sections.html:
1. Have a title company or attorney draft the deed to the formatting rules, with the 3-inch top margin and the legal description on page one.
  2. Sign it, with a name printed under every signature.
  3. Call (816) 858-3326 for the exact total, since overpayments are not refunded.
  4. Deliver the deed to Room 035 between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m. on a weekday, or mail it to the address above.
  5. Register for the free Record Notification Service so you hear when the deed is recorded.

In a cash sale the steps are the same. With no lender, the title company usually sends the deed in on closing day, so confirm who is delivering it and by what hour.

faqs.q: What does the first page of a standard deed cost?
faqs.a: It costs $26.00, and every added page costs $3.00. A document that misses the formatting standards costs $51.00 for the first page.

faqs.q: When can I file a document with the Platte County recorder?
faqs.a: Bring it between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m. on a weekday. The office stays open from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. for searches and copies.

faqs.q: What address do I use to send a deed for recording?
faqs.a: Use the Recorder of Deeds, 415 Third St., Room 035, Platte City, MO 64079. Call (816) 858-3326 to confirm the total, because overpayments are not refunded.

faqs.q: How can I be told when a deed is recorded?
faqs.a: Register for a free account at plattemo.icounty.com and set your criteria in the Record Notification Service. The system emails you when a matching deed reaches the office.

faqs.q: Does the Platte County recorder file UCC statements?
faqs.a: No. The Missouri Secretary of State has taken UCC filings since July 1, 2001. A real estate fixture filing on the approved form with the required addendum is priced at $26.00 for the first page.
